_comment: Months and weekdays drawn as a calendar page, not searched for and not clozed (tunatale-xykz, the user 2026-09-28). Each word in `words` maps to a language-neutral concept in app.cards.calendar_scenes.CALENDAR_CONCEPTS: `month_1`..`month_12` then `weekday_1`..`weekday_7` in ISO order, where 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. A photo search CANNOT serve this vocabulary at all: asked for 'marso' it returns a march of people, asked for 'lunes' a photograph of a desk. What these words name is a POSITION in a structure, so the picture is the structure — a year as a 4x3 grid, a week as a row of seven — with the one cell the word points at lit. `week_start` is DATA, in this file, because which day opens a week is a local custom rather than a fact about calendars: Cebuano and Tagalog open on Sunday, which is the common Philippine printed calendar layout, while Norwegian and Slovene open on Monday. It is read from here by app.cards.calendar_picture.load_calendar and handed to the renderer as an argument, so the renderer's own copy of the order cannot make the test pass; it is also in every picture's FILENAME, because a Sunday-first week draws a different page for the same concept and a shared name would serve this deck's Monday card the European one. A word in `words` is NOT a function word, whatever `function_words.json` or a POS tag says, so a month never goes down the cloze route its UPOS would otherwise pick. The veto is asked about a bare token and cannot see a SENSE, so the picture is drawn only when the card's English gloss names the month or the day. The Cebuano day names are the Spanish ones throughout (`lunes`, `martes`, `domingo`), so the gloss is also the only confirmation available — a picture cannot print the word on the row, or the card would be answerable by reading it. This file is keyed to the Bisaya deck's spellings; it has not been native-checked (tunatale-u8nz.9 covers the other Cebuano data files the same way). Only the primary spellings are listed, so every word maps to exactly one concept.
